reader.title: Lynching of Frank Lucky
bases: A Black prisoner was taken from a jail and hanged to a tree by unnamed persons (A1, A2).

Frank Lucky was taken from jail and hanged, an extralegal killing of a prisoner (A1, A2), but neither report names the perpetrators, their number, or the charge he was held on, so the group size and pretext are not stated.
A Memphis item (A1, reprinted verbatim in A3) and a differently worded Austin item (A2) agree on the core event, though both may derive from a common Texas exchange report.

summary.text: The lynching of Frank Lucky was the hanging of a Black prisoner who was taken from the jail at Wortham, Texas, one night in early October 1881.
The killing survives only in brief news paragraphs in Texas and Tennessee papers, which gave no cause and closed with jokes on the victim's surname.
According to the Austin Weekly Democratic Statesman of October 13, "a negro named Frank Lucky" was taken from the jail at Wortham "one night last week and hanged to a tree."
The Memphis Daily Appeal, two days earlier, said he had been taken from the jail at "Wertham" and "hung recently."
Neither paper named the people who removed him, said how many there were, or stated the charge on which he had been held.
No report of an inquest, arrest, or other official response appears in the coverage.
The Memphis Appeal ran the item in its "Neighborhood News" miscellany, between a report on a compromised abduction trial and a note on Kentucky coal lands.
It ended with a quip that if Lucky "can wonder at all now, he will wonder what there is in a name, anyhow."
The Bolivar Bulletin in Tennessee reprinted the Memphis paragraph word for word on October 20 among general paragraphs.
In Texas, the Austin Statesman placed the hanging in a column of state news, beside items on cotton picking and railroad building.
Its version added the night-time seizure and the tree, and it closed with the line "He was not very lucky."
None of the three papers commented on the legality of the hanging or on who was responsible.
The town's name was printed "Wertham" in the Memphis item and "Wortham" in the Texas paper, whose spelling is more likely correct since the item ran in its state news column.
